$comment: CW Operating Procedure (#294, #295), pinned for all three ports:
Read by ios/Sources/MorseKitCheck/main.swift and by OperatingProcedureTest.kt
Every expected value below was worked out by hand from the rules in
'derivation' and docs/operating-procedure-design.md, not captured from any
port. Do not regenerate it to make a failing test pass; change it only when
a rule is meant to change.

rules: Lessons, in order: offset, signals, when, once, partial, me, exchange, mistake (offsetting first, straight after First Four: maintainer, 2026-10-03).

normalizeCall / normalizeState: upper-case and remove every whitespace character. Valid call: 3-10 characters of A-Z 0-9 '/', at least one letter and one digit. Valid state: 2-3 letters A-Z. prefillCall: the normalised call, or '' when it is W1AW (the settings placeholder).
The activator is the first row of the activator table whose call is not the learner's; the other hunter likewise over the other-hunter table.

Choices are listed primary right answer first. 'accepted' lists every choice index that counts as right; when it is absent only index 0 does. A choice is {send: text}, {silent: true} or {option: key}. A scenario is an 'action' scenario when every choice is send or silent.
shift(c, n): a letter steps through A-Z and a digit through 0-9 by n, wrapping; anything else is unchanged. 'Moved on one' is shift 1, 'moved back six' is shift -6.

partialMatches(partial, call): upper-case, remove whitespace, strip every trailing '?'. Empty -> true (a bare '?' is everyone's). Otherwise true when what is left occurs as one contiguous run inside the normalised call.
notMinePartial(call): the call up to and including its first digit, with that digit replaced by (digit + 2) mod 10; while the result occurs in the call, add 1 more (mod 10). Then append '?'.
nearMiss(call): the first letter after the call's first digit, shifted -6; if there is no letter after the first digit, the call's last letter instead.

Partials used by the partial-calls lesson: prefix = first two characters + '?'; suffix = last two characters + '?'; fullCall = every character but the last + '?', whose missing part is the last character.

Mistake texts (lesson 'mistake'): call = call with its last character shifted 1; last = call with its last character shifted -6; state = '5NN ' + state with its last letter shifted 1. 'hear' plays the shifted call, an error, then the activator's acknowledgement of the real call.

Reply (primary, First Four's) = '5NN ' + state + ' 73'. ReplyBK (WB0RLJ's order, accepted too) = '5NN ' + state + ' BK', and after the activator's 'TU 73 E E' the close '73 E E' (accepted beside 'E E'). Ragchew = '<A> DE <C> TNX FER CALL UR 5NN 5NN NAME JOE QTH <S> <S> HW? <A> DE <C> KN'.

An error is written <ERR> (any shape, chosen when it plays) or <ERR:n> (row n of errorVariants, mod its count). It is not a prosign. clipParts splits a text on single spaces into runs of words and errors; display() joins the parts with single spaces, each error shown as errorDisplay. An error variant plays count dits at the learner's speed times speed: run together (element gaps) or as separate dits (character gaps).
Pileup demo: callers in mix order W8KDP, KE0RJ, you, AB7TF, N4LQX; a caller equal to the learner's call becomes KC2VWM. wpm = max(5, learner wpm + delta); pitch = max(200, tone + offset).
heardPitch(tone, station, vfo, rit) = tone + station - (vfo + rit). transmitOffset(station, vfo, xit) = vfo + xit - station. isZeroBeat(x) = |x| <= zeroBeatToleranceHz. audible(p) = max(200, p).

Drill: round n starts at drillStarts[n mod count]; an answer is right when isZeroBeat(transmitOffset(start, vfo, 0)). zeroBeatStreakToPass right in a row passes the drill; a miss sets the streak to 0.

A scenario run answers each scenario once, in order; an answer is right when its index is accepted. A wrong answer is a mistake and still moves on. The run is clean when finished with no mistakes. Answers after the end change nothing and return false.

Progress: recordRun(lesson, clean) adds the lesson to cleanRuns when clean. A lesson passes when it has a clean run and, for 'offset' only, the drill has passed too. nextLesson is the first lesson in order that has not passed; null when all have.

Is it me? (maintainer, 2026-10-03): a near-miss of your call without '?' (they are working that station) means stay silent; the near-miss with '?' means send your call once and listen for whether they correct to yours.

choices.send: K4RTZ DE N9HO TNX FER CALL UR 5NN 5NN NAME JOE QTH WI WI HW? K4RTZ DE N9HO KN

lines.text: K4RTZ DE N9HO TNX FER CALL UR 5NN 5NN NAME JOE QTH WI WI HW? K4RTZ DE N9HO KN

choices.send: W0PQA DE K4RTZ TNX FER CALL UR 5NN 5NN NAME JOE QTH VA VA HW? W0PQA DE K4RTZ KN

runs.$comment: The second answer is wrong; the run still moves on. The fifth answer comes after the end and returns false.
Either exchange form is right (indices 0 and 1); answering mistake.hear with your call again is not.
